w10_T4_013308: Maria started her day with 56 dollars. In the morning, she spent 12 dollars on coffee. By afternoon, she earned 54 dollars from tutoring. She spent 82 dollars at the store. That evening, she lost 1 dollar on the street. Her friend gave her 41 dollars. Later, she found 19 dollars in her old coat. How many dollars does Maria have at the end of the day?
w10_T4_013313: A book club began with 177 books. They sold 58 books at a garage sale. Then they purchased 66 new books. They gave away 171 books to a library. Seven books were damaged and discarded. Finally, they received a donation of 68 books. How many books does the club have now?
w10_T4_013324: Sarah has 98 apples. After selling 73 apples at the farmers market, she had triple the remaining amount picked by her friend. Then she sold 75 more and ended with 6 times that amount from another harvest. How many apples does Sarah have in total?
w10_T4_013339: A factory started with 130 units. In the morning, production multiplied output by 9 times. By afternoon, it multiplied by 9 times again. Then 3,005 units were shipped out. Later, 7,284 units were removed for quality control. Finally, 17 units were recovered. How many units remain in the factory?
w10_T4_013345: A farm had 59 liters of milk. The morning collection produced 4 times as much. They added 18 more liters from a second collection. They sold 98 liters at the market. By evening, the remaining amount was multiplied 8 times when combined with stored reserves. How many liters does the farm have?
w10_T4_013349: A bakery started with 206 cookies. They baked 6 times as many by noon. They sold 303 cookies. Then they baked 32 more. They received a delivery of 73 cookies. Finally, they packaged all remaining cookies 5 at a time. How many packages did they make?
w10_T4_013350: A tree starts with 52 pieces of fruit. Over time, it gained 14 more pieces. Then it produced 7 times as much. It produced 7 times as much again. Farmers added 62 more pieces. Finally, all fruit was bundled in groups of 6. How many bundles were created?
w10_T4_013356: A store had 122 items. In the morning, they received 5 times as many items. They sold 372 items. They received 30 more items. Then they grouped all remaining items 8 at a time. Finally, they removed 979 grouped items. How many individual items were left?
w10_T4_013364: A classroom had 29 pencils at the start. In the morning, there were 3 times as many. At midday, they distributed pencils equally among 3 students. After the lesson, 18 pencils were missing. Then there were 3 times as many from a new box. Finally, 55 more were added. How many pencils are in the classroom?
w10_T4_013369: A sports team scored 145 points in the first half. They divided the score equally among 5 games played so far. In the next game, they lost 19 points due to penalties. They lost 7 more points. Then they multiplied their remaining points by 9 for a tournament bonus. Then they multiplied by 4 again. Finally, they earned 19 bonus points. What was their final tournament score?
w10_T4_013370: Two players counted 206 marbles together. Player A took half of them. Then Player A added 45 marbles from home. He added 40 more marbles. But then 85 marbles were lost during a game. How many marbles does Player A have now?
w10_T4_013371: A factory worker started with 179 boxes. They removed 21 boxes in the morning. They removed 34 more boxes by afternoon. They grouped the remaining boxes equally into 4 shipments. Then they added 61 boxes to each shipment. What is the count per shipment (in terms of boxes, considering all changes)?
w10_T4_013376: A carpenter had 188 nails. After using half of them on a project, 188 ÷ 2 nails remained. He added 46 nails from his supply. He tripled the amount for a larger project. Then he used 387 nails and had 2 nails break. Finally, he grouped the remaining 5 per package. How many packages did he make?
w10_T4_013378: A team started with 144 points. They gained 12 points in round 1. They multiplied their points by 5 in round 2. They multiplied by 7 in the final championship. Then they divided the total equally by 2 teams. What were the final points per team?
w10_T4_013380: A factory produced 168 items on day 1. On day 2, production tripled. They added 15 more items from inventory. On day 3, they shipped out 435 items. On day 4, remaining items were multiplied 7 times. Then they divided into 3 equal shipments. How many items per shipment?
w10_T4_013383: Player A had 86 coins. He multiplied his coins 6 times through a lucky event. He gained 41 more coins. He lost 326 coins in a wager. Afterwards, his remaining coins were multiplied 7 times. How many coins does Player A have?
w10_T4_013384: A recipe called for 41 grams of flour. After removing 22 grams, the baker tripled the mixture for larger batches. It was tripled again. Then it was tripled once more. Finally, 13 grams of salt were added. What is the total weight now?
w10_T4_013386: A warehouse had 110 boxes. In the morning, stock multiplied by 7. By afternoon, 676 boxes were sold. Later, the remaining stock multiplied by 5. Then it multiplied by 7 again. How many boxes are in the warehouse?
w10_T4_013387: Sarah had 145 stickers. She multiplied her collection 8 times. Then she divided equally among 5 friends. Then she multiplied the amount by 2. Finally, she divided by 2 again. How many stickers does each friend have?
w10_T4_013390: A garden started with 51 plants. The first season, 35 were added, making it grow 7 times. Then 67 plants were added. This stock multiplied 6 times. Then it multiplied 9 times. What is the total number of plants (in thousands)?
w10_T4_013393: A school started with 143 students. By fall, enrollment doubled: 143 × 9. By winter, enrollment grew 4 times. By spring, enrollment divided into 2 equal halves. Four more students enrolled. Two students left. What is the enrollment drop?
w10_T4_013394: A restaurant started with 78 meals. They subtracted 66 meals sold by noon. They multiplied the remaining by 6. They added 6 more meals. They multiplied by 5. Then they multiplied by 9. How many meals does the restaurant have?
w10_T4_013396: A library started with 51 books. After removing 32 books, they multiplied the collection 4 times. They multiplied by 7 again. Then they sold 443 books. They multiplied the remainder 4 times. How many books remain?
w10_T4_013406: A store had 138 items. In the morning, 2 items were damaged. Then they received 16 items. They tripled the stock. They added 59 more items. They added another 21 items. How many items does the store have?
w10_T4_013409: A team started with 113 points. They gained 71 points in the first match. They multiplied their score 5 times for a tournament multiplier. They scored 375 more points. Finally, they earned 39 bonus points. What is the team's final score?
